column1: # Refreshed measured rows from CI run 37589416238 (2026-10-07).
# Passed, full-scope items >= 0.1 minutes replace their previous estimates;
# other rows retain their earlier provenance below. The formal-tlc*
# deterministic rows were re-measured for #5166 from two receipt-free
# exhaustive runs; see the lattice section below.
# Per-work-item duration estimates, in minutes, used only to bin-pack the
# matrix. Format: package<TAB>shard<TAB>tier<TAB>minutes, with `-` for the
# shard of an unsharded package and `all` for its single untiered invocation.
# A missing row falls back to DEFAULT_ESTIMATE in plan-test-matrix.py, so this
# file can never make the plan wrong - only less well balanced.
# PROVENANCE. Every row in the original median refresh was MEASURED; later
# refreshes below have their own provenance.
# Each original figure is the MEDIAN wall-clock of that work item
# across every successful pull-request run of ci.yml created between
# 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-28: 85 successful runs, of which 67 still carried
# leg-results artifacts and 49 were full fan-outs (46-47 packages, `lattice`
# included). Each item has between 35 and 67 samples. The figure is the time
# the item took on its leg - test time plus that invocation's own process
# start - read from the per-leg `leg-results-*` records that run-test-leg.py
# writes, taking the highest attempt per leg. The aggregate report still emits
# single-run rows in exactly this format at the end of every run, so a quick
# refresh from one run remains a copy-paste.
# A single run's figure is accurate to roughly +/- 30%, because that is what
# consecutive green runs of the same commit actually vary by on shared runners
# (`lattice.replication` ranged 1.9 - 4.2 min over this window, and
# `lattice.api.mcp.repocontext / host` 1.4 - 4.6). That is well inside what
# bin-packing needs - the packer is choosing which leg to put an item on, not
# predicting a deadline. The median is used for this refresh because the window
# was available, not because single-run rows are unfit: the error that matters
# is an order-of-magnitude one, and it comes from staleness, not sampling.
# Measured against the same 49 fan-outs, the previous rows planned a leg set
# whose longest leg ran a median 6.96 min of test time (7.1 min observed on
# average); replaying the same samples through these rows plans one whose
# longest leg is 6.0 min, against a 5.9 min lower bound of total/legs. The
# rows that had drifted most were `lattice.dashboards` (3.3 -> 4.7),
# STALENESS IS THE FAILURE MODE, and it is silent. Before this refresh these
# rows were a full epic behind: `lattice.api.mcp.repocontext` was recorded at
# 2.7 min against a measured 10.7, `lattice / rest (deterministic)` at 0.4
# against 3.4, and `lattice.dashboards` at 0.0 against 2.5. Nothing failed -
# the packer simply planned around a suite that no longer existed and put the
# longest item in the matrix on a leg it had priced as cheap. Refresh this file
# from the aggregate report whenever a package's test surface grows in earnest.
# Staleness costs more than leg balance, which is the part that is easy to
# miss. `pack()` caps the leg count at `total / largest + 1`, so an item whose
# real duration dwarfs its recorded one does not merely land on the wrong leg -
# once the estimates are honest it SUPPRESSES THE FAN-OUT, because one 10.7 min
# item against a 65 min total admits only six legs however many runners the
# matrix is allowed. Understating an item hides that; correcting it surfaces a
# suite that needs sharding. Both effects are invisible from a green run.
# The zero rows are real and are deliberately kept. A sharded package crossed
# with the tiers has tiers with no tests in them at all - `primitives` has no
# chaos fixtures, `bplustree-chaos` has no deterministic ones. Each such item
# still costs one `dotnet test` process start, and recording it as 0.0 does not
# hide that: the packer adds PER_ITEM_OVERHEAD to every item on top of its
# estimate, so a leg carrying five empty items is correctly priced above one
# They are not pruned, and that is the deliberate choice rather than an
# oversight. Pruning would mean deciding ahead of time that a (shard, tier)
# pair is empty, which is true today and is exactly the kind of fact that
# stops being true the moment somebody adds the first chaos fixture to
# Primitives. The tests would then simply stop running, with nothing to say
# so: the vacuity guard fires when a shard is empty across every tier, so it
# would not catch a single tier silently disappearing from a shard that is
# otherwise busy. Those 18 empty items measure 0.04 min each, about 0.7 min of
# aggregate overhead spread across ten legs, and that buys the property that a new fixture is picked up wherever it lands.
# A package that sets "crossTiers": false in test-shards.json has no such rows
# to keep: its shards are not crossed with the tiers, so each one contributes a
# single `all` row and there is no empty tier to price.
# The formal-tlc* deterministic rows are not medians. Each is the mean of
# two measured item durations (leg-results `duration`, the time the item took
# on its leg), rounded up to hundredths of a minute, re-measured for #5166
# after controls became shared by content (#5152) and base-served (#5161):
# - ci.yml bucket push run 40909619830 (head 9418a498d), receipt-free, so
#   every TLC module ran exhaustively on the ten-leg plan;
#   dispatch whose eight exhaustive TLC legs run uninstrumented.
# Both runs passed every TLC case. The two samples agree within about 5% on
# most shards, but a single case can vary 1.5x between runs on identical
# inputs: the dedicated TwoPartitions item took 35.22 and 52.78 minutes, and
# scheduling-workload-b 12.11 and 20.64. The mean prices that noise, it does
# not remove it. formal-tlc-bplus-cascade replaces three shards (#5166); its
# row is the sum of their measured items, an upper bound once the base serves
# the mutation controls. Estimates are planning inputs, not runtime
# guarantees, and they decide only how work is distributed, never what runs.
# formal-tlc-view-numeric (#5232): one sample, its 23 cases on leg 6 of
# formal-tlc-schema-view (#5233): its 26 cases took 1.3 minutes locally at
# LATTICE_TLC_CONCURRENCY=2; doubled until measured on its member PR's CI leg.
# formal-tlc-schema is one measured item. Its 30 SchemaPolicyConfig and
# SchemaStageOrdering cases took 2.34 minutes in the receipt-free member pull
# with SchemaVersionFamily's 18 cases added, all 48 ran (no schema receipt) in
# 1 m 54 s of dotnet test in ci.yml run 41087582284 (head e15b3091e, job
# SchemaComplianceScan's 38 cases added to the first two modules, all 68 took
# 6.64 minutes (dotnet test 6 m 34 s) in ci.yml run 41088681728 (head
# (#5228) add 0.78 minutes measured locally (16-core Windows workstation); the
# row adds them to that figure until the #5228 member run measures all 104.
# lattice/rest (deterministic) uses complete passing item TRX from green run
# time excludes some process overhead, and the price rounds up once to
# hundredths. Historical run 40576287689 (head 6a008512) had the atomic leg-4
# orphan-slot flake (#5112); its lattice/rest item from that failed leg is
# excluded. The earlier replacement came from green run 40588531777 (head
# Every category-routed formal-tlc-* shard runs only the deterministic tier
